LESSON: AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: LISTENING AND SPEAKING
Topic 1.1: Auditory discrimination
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Auditory discrimination, part of LISTENING AND SPEAKING in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Which letter sounds almost sound the same? a) 2. Which animal sounds do you hear within our school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Auditory discrimination together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: Listening keenly and actively as the learner listens to letter sounds articulation

from the teacher or an audio recording/video clip.

57

• Creativity and imagination: Imagination and originality as the leaner take a nature walk within the neighbourhood to

listen to sounds made by animals

Values:
• Integrity is enhanced as the learner works to complete assigned roles.

• Unity is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with others to play letter sound games.

58

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Animal welfare education is enhanced as the learner learns to care for animals.

Link to other Activity Areas: environmental activities as learner identify sounds of animals in the environment as they

identify sounds of animals kept at home.

Suggested learning resources: Book, audio books shelves, bags, tables, chart on animals, flash cards, adapted digital devices,

adapted pencils, page turners, cards, books, book holders, letter puzzle
